meta.title: Government of India - Education Schemes Database (enriched)
meta.description: education_schemes.json enriched with machine-filterable fields so a frontend can run eligibility matching. Original 17 fields preserved verbatim.
meta.disclaimer: Scheme rules, benefit amounts, income ceilings, and portal URLs change periodically (and with union budgets each year). Verify against the official ministry/scheme websites before using figures in production, especially anything user-facing.

derived_rules.education_level: Mapped from class/level wording already present in the source description and eligibility fields.
derived_rules.aid_type: Assigned from the benefit described in coverage_amount.
derived_rules.application_required: Assigned from how the source says a beneficiary is enrolled or paid (e.g. 'no separate application required' -> none).
derived_rules.benefits_individual: false where coverage_amount is a programme/institutional outlay rather than a benefit to one person.
derived_rules.max_income: Only set where a rupee figure was already written in the source eligibility/coverage text. Never inferred.
derived_rules.min_marks_pct: Only set where a percentage was already written in the source.

data_quality.not_yet_available_note: These fields are required by the website spec but appear nowhere in education_schemes.json. They are NOT invented here. Source them from the National Scholarship Portal (scholarships.gov.in) and each scheme's official site, then set last_verified_date. Until then the frontend must not render an Apply button or a deadline countdown for any scheme.

income_criterion_legend.limit-known: A rupee income ceiling exists in the source text and is recorded in max_income.
income_criterion_legend.no-limit: The source describes the scheme as income-independent or universal. No ceiling applies.
income_criterion_legend.unstated: The source refers to an income criterion but gives no figure. max_income is null and the frontend must NOT claim eligibility.
income_criterion_legend.not-applicable: Institutional, infrastructure or policy entry with no individual income test.

filter_vocabulary.income_band_matching_rule: A scheme matches a band when scheme.max_income >= band.max. income_criterion 'no-limit' always matches. income_criterion 'unstated' never matches a specific band and is only shown when the user opts in, because the dataset does not record a figure. 'prefer-not' behaves like 'any' but is remembered as an explicit user choice.

disability_legend.eligible: The source text explicitly names disability provision (reservation, stipend, or adapted content).
disability_legend.unstated: No disability provision is mentioned. This is NOT the same as 'not eligible' - it means the dataset is silent. Only three schemes in this dataset name a disability provision.

area_labels.Scholarship - Social Category (SC/ST/OBC: Scholarship — Social Category (SC / ST / OBC / Minority)

filter_vocabulary.axis_note: Two independent groupings share the word 'category'. They must not be confused. 'area' is record.category: the thematic area a scheme belongs to. 'beneficiary' is filter.category: the social category a scheme is restricted to, or ['all'] when it is open to everyone. Filtering by one never implies the other.

schemes.name: Samagra Shiksha Abhiyan
schemes.ministry: Ministry of Education (Dept. of School Education and Literacy)
schemes.description: Integrated scheme for school education from pre-school to senior secondary level, subsuming earlier schemes SSA, RMSA, and Teacher Education. Largest school-education programme in the central budget.
schemes.coverage_amount: Rs. 42,100 crore allocation for 2026-27 (programme-level, not individual benefit)
schemes.eligibility: All government and government-aided schools; students from pre-school through Class XII
schemes.target_beneficiaries: School-going children across pre-primary to senior secondary levels nationwide
key_features: Improves school infrastructure
Free textbooks and uniforms for eligible students
Stipends and accessible facilities for children with disabilities (CWSN)
Teacher training and residential school funding
Subsumes Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan (SSA), RMSA, and Teacher Education schemes

filter.disability_basis: Key feature states 'Stipends and accessible facilities for children with disabilities (CWSN)'.

schemes.name: PM POSHAN (erstwhile Mid-Day Meal Scheme)
schemes.ministry: Ministry of Education (Dept. of School Education and Literacy)
schemes.description: Provides one hot cooked meal to children studying in Classes I-VIII in government and government-aided schools, aimed at improving nutritional status and encouraging regular school attendance.
schemes.coverage_amount: Rs. 12,750 crore allocation for 2026-27 (programme-level)
schemes.eligibility: Automatic for all children enrolled in Classes I-VIII at participating government/government-aided schools; no separate application required
schemes.target_beneficiaries: Children in Classes I-VIII in government and government-aided schools
key_features: Renamed from 'Mid-Day Meal Scheme' to 'PM POSHAN' in 2021
Free hot cooked meal on all school working days
Also covers micronutrient supplementation and health check-ups in convergence with other programmes

schemes.name: National Means-cum-Merit Scholarship Scheme
schemes.ministry: Ministry of Education (Dept. of School Education and Literacy)
schemes.description: Awards scholarships to meritorious students from economically weaker sections to prevent dropout after Class VIII and support continued education through Class XII.
schemes.coverage_amount: Rs. 12,000 per year (Rs. 1,000/month), payable from Class IX to XII
schemes.eligibility: Minimum 55% marks in Class VII (relaxable for SC/ST) to appear for selection test; minimum 55% in Class VIII; parental income up to Rs. 3.5 lakh per annum; studying in government/government-aided/local-body schools
schemes.target_beneficiaries: Meritorious students from economically weaker sections entering Class IX
key_features: 100,000 scholarships awarded annually nationwide
State-level selection test required
Disbursed via Public Financial Management System (PFMS)/DBT
Applied for via National Scholarship Portal (scholarships.gov.in)
_review: max_income 350000 derived verbatim from eligibility text 'parental income up to Rs. 3.5 lakh per annum'. Income ceilings are revised periodically - re-verify each budget cycle.
min_marks_pct 55 derived from 'Minimum 55% marks in Class VII'. Note the source also states a relaxable rule for SC/ST which is not represented numerically here.

schemes.name: Pradhan Mantri Uchchatar Shiksha Protsahan Yojana
schemes.ministry: Ministry of Education (Dept. of Higher Education)
schemes.description: Provides financial assistance to meritorious students from economically weaker backgrounds pursuing undergraduate and postgraduate courses, and also encompasses the Central Sector Interest Subsidy (CSIS) component for education loans.
schemes.coverage_amount: Rs. 12,000/year for first 3 years of UG courses; Rs. 20,000/year for PG courses
schemes.eligibility: Above 80 percentile in Class XII board exam; family income below Rs. 4.5 lakh per annum; admission in AICTE/UGC-recognised institutions
schemes.target_beneficiaries: Meritorious economically weaker undergraduate/postgraduate students
key_features: Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) to student bank accounts
Includes Central Sector Interest Subsidy (CSIS) on education loans for full interest waiver during moratorium
Applied for via National Scholarship Portal
_review: max_income 450000 derived verbatim from eligibility text 'family income below Rs. 4.5 lakh per annum'.
min_percentile_xii 80 derived from 'Above 80 percentile in Class XII board exam'.
CSIS is recorded as a component here AND as its own record (PMMVY-EDU-NOTE). A user matching PM-USP will see CSIS as a related duplicate. Consider linking rather than listing both.

schemes.name: PM Vidyalaxmi Scheme
schemes.ministry: Ministry of Education (Dept. of Higher Education)
schemes.description: Mission-mode scheme providing collateral-free, guarantor-free education loans to students admitted on merit to Quality Higher Educational Institutions (QHEIs), with interest subvention for lower-income families, stemming from NEP 2020.
schemes.coverage_amount: Loans up to Rs. 7.5 lakh with 75% government credit guarantee; 3% interest subvention on loans up to Rs. 10 lakh for family income up to Rs. 8 lakh/year
schemes.eligibility: Indian students admitted on merit (not management/NRI quota) to one of 1,425+ designated QHEIs; interest subvention requires valid income certificate; benefit usable once per UG/PG/integrated course
schemes.target_beneficiaries: Students admitted to top-tier higher educational institutions (over 22 lakh students/year targeted)
key_features: Single online portal for education loan applications across multiple banks
Collateral-free and guarantor-free loans
Interest capped at bank's EBLR + 0.5%, with further concession for interest-servicing during study
Tax benefit on interest paid under Section 80E
Approved by Union Cabinet on 6 November 2024
_review: max_income 800000 is the ceiling for the 3% interest subvention ONLY, not for the loan itself. Loans up to Rs. 7.5 lakh are available without that income test. Treating 800000 as a single max_income will wrongly hide the loan from users above Rs. 8 lakh. Model these as two separate benefits before shipping.
QHEI count (1,425+) and annual target (22 lakh) are volatile. Re-verify on vidyalakshmi.co.in.

schemes.name: Rashtriya Uchchatar Shiksha Abhiyan
schemes.ministry: Ministry of Education (Dept. of Higher Education)
schemes.description: Aims to improve access, equity and quality in state higher education institutions through strategic funding, based on norm-based and performance-linked criteria.
schemes.coverage_amount: Institutional grants (not an individual student benefit)
schemes.eligibility: State public universities and colleges meeting RUSA norms
schemes.target_beneficiaries: State universities and colleges, and by extension their students
key_features: Funding linked to academic, administrative and governance reforms
Support for new model colleges, infrastructure upgrades, and quality improvement
Focus on equity for disadvantaged regions and groups
_review: Not an individual-benefit scheme. Excluded from student-facing results by default; shown only when the user enables 'Show institutional and policy schemes'.

schemes.name: PM Young Achievers Scholarship Award Scheme for Vibrant India (PM-YASASVI)
schemes.ministry: Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
schemes.description: Provides scholarships to meritorious students from Other Backward Classes (OBC), Economically Backward Classes (EBC), and Denotified, Nomadic and Semi-Nomadic Tribes (DNT/NT/SNT) to support their studies from Class IX through higher education.
schemes.coverage_amount: Varies by stage - pre-matric, post-matric (Class XI-XII) and top-class college components, generally in the range of Rs. 12,000-1,25,000+ per year depending on level
schemes.eligibility: Students belonging to OBC, EBC, DNT/NT/SNT categories; family income limits apply and vary by scheme component
schemes.target_beneficiaries: Meritorious students from OBC/EBC/DNT/NT/SNT backgrounds
key_features: Covers pre-matric, post-matric, and 'Top Class' (premier institution) tiers
Selection via YASASVI Entrance Test (YET) for some components
Applied for via National Scholarship Portal
_review: CRITICAL: max_income is null because the source says 'family income limits apply and vary by scheme component' without giving figures. The income filter will not match this scheme. Source the three component ceilings from scholarships.gov.in before launch.
official_website points to yet.nta.ac.in (the entrance test portal) but applications run on scholarships.gov.in. Consider using both.

schemes.name: Top Class Education Scheme for OBC, EBC and DNT Students
schemes.ministry: Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
schemes.description: Provides full financial support to meritorious OBC, EBC and DNT students admitted to identified premier higher education institutions for professional and technical courses.
schemes.coverage_amount: Full tuition fee up to Rs. 2 lakh/year; accommodation up to Rs. 3,000/month; books/stationery allowance up to Rs. 5,000/year; one-time laptop grant up to Rs. 45,000
schemes.eligibility: Family income up to Rs. 2.5 lakh/year (OBC/DNT) or Rs. 1 lakh/year (EBC); admission via merit to a listed premier institution
schemes.target_beneficiaries: Meritorious OBC/EBC/DNT students at premier institutions
key_features: Covers full tuition and near-complete cost of living at listed institutions
One-time laptop/device grant
Applied for via National Scholarship Portal
_review: max_income 250000 is the OBC/DNT ceiling. EBC ceiling is 100000. A single max_income cannot express both - a user selecting EBC could be shown a scheme they exceed. Consider income_ceiling_by_category.
The Rs. 45,000 laptop grant is one-time, not annual.

schemes.name: National Fellowship and Scholarship for Higher Education of ST Students
schemes.ministry: Ministry of Tribal Affairs
schemes.description: Provides fellowships and scholarships to Scheduled Tribe (ST) students for pursuing higher education, including M.Phil and Ph.D. programmes.
schemes.coverage_amount: Fellowship amount aligned with UGC's NET-JRF rates for research scholars; separate scholarship components for professional/technical courses
schemes.eligibility: ST students admitted to recognised universities/institutions for post-graduate and doctoral studies
schemes.target_beneficiaries: Scheduled Tribe students pursuing higher/research education
key_features: Covers M.Phil/Ph.D. research fellowships
Applied for via National Scholarship Portal
_review: id is PM-YOUNG-ACHIEVERS-ST but short_name is NFST and the name is 'National Fellowship and Scholarship... of ST Students'. The id appears to be a copy-paste error carried over from the PM-YASASVI record. Recommend renaming the id to NFST.
Source states no income ceiling. income_criterion is unstated - confirm whether an income test applies to the fellowship component.

schemes.name: Post Matric Scholarship Scheme for SC Students
schemes.ministry: Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
schemes.description: Provides financial assistance to Scheduled Caste students studying at post-matriculation or post-secondary stage to reduce the economic burden of higher education.
schemes.coverage_amount: Maintenance allowance and reimbursement of compulsory non-refundable fees, varying by course and institution type
schemes.eligibility: SC students studying in Class XI and above; family income ceiling applies (revised periodically)
schemes.target_beneficiaries: Scheduled Caste students in post-matric/higher education
key_features: One of India's oldest scholarship schemes
Covers maintenance allowance, tuition and other compulsory fees
Applied for via National Scholarship Portal
_review: CRITICAL: source says 'family income ceiling applies (revised periodically)' with no figure. This is one of the most-used SC schemes, so an unstated ceiling means the income filter silently hides it from most users. Source the current ceiling from scholarships.gov.in.
The source eligibility says 'Class XI and above' but the scheme is named Post Matric. Verify the starting class.

schemes.name: Beti Bachao Beti Padhao
schemes.ministry: Ministry of Women and Child Development
schemes.implementing_body: Ministry of Women and Child Development, Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, Ministry of Education
schemes.description: National flagship programme addressing the declining child sex ratio and promoting the survival, protection and education of the girl child through multi-sectoral convergence.
schemes.coverage_amount: Not applicable (advocacy, convergence and sectoral schemes)
schemes.eligibility: Universal - focus on girl children nationwide, especially in gender-critical districts
schemes.target_beneficiaries: Girl children and their families
key_features: Media/community advocacy against sex-selective practices
Convergence with health and education sector schemes
Implemented initially in gender-critical districts, later expanded nationwide
_review: Advocacy programme, not a benefit scheme. Should not appear in 'scholarships you can apply for' results. Grouped under girl-child schemes but points users to Sukanya Samriddhi for the actual monetary product.

schemes.name: Sukanya Samriddhi Yojana
schemes.ministry: Ministry of Finance (Dept. of Economic Affairs)
schemes.scheme_type: Small Savings Scheme (under Beti Bachao Beti Padhao)
schemes.description: Government-backed small savings scheme encouraging parents to build a fund for a girl child's future education and marriage expenses, offering a high tax-free interest rate.
schemes.coverage_amount: Deposits from Rs. 250 to Rs. 1,50,000 per year; interest rate set quarterly by government (historically among the highest small-savings rates)
schemes.eligibility: Account can be opened by parents/guardian for a girl child from birth until she turns 10 years
schemes.target_beneficiaries: Girl children (via parent/guardian-operated savings account)
key_features: Tax-exempt under Section 80C (EEE status)
Account matures after 21 years or on marriage after age 18
Partial withdrawal permitted for higher education expenses after age 18
_review: Beneficiary is a girl child, but the applicant is a parent/guardian. Add an applicant_type field if you want to separate 'student searching' from 'parent saving' journeys.
The interest rate is reset quarterly by government and is NOT stored in this record. Display it from India Post / RBI at render time or the card will show a stale rate.
Deposit ceiling (Rs. 1.5 lakh/yr) is frequently revised - re-verify.

schemes.name: CBSE Single Girl Child Scholarship Scheme
schemes.ministry: Ministry of Education (via CBSE)
schemes.description: Scholarship for single girl children (only child of parents) who score well in Class X CBSE board exams, to support their Class XI-XII studies.
schemes.coverage_amount: Rs. 500 per month for two years (Class XI and XII)
schemes.eligibility: Girl student who is the only child of her parents; minimum 60% aggregate marks in CBSE Class X; continuing studies in a CBSE-affiliated school
schemes.target_beneficiaries: Single girl children pursuing Class XI-XII
key_features: Renewed annually subject to minimum 60% marks in Class XI to continue into Class XII
Applied for through the school/CBSE regional office
_review: No income condition in the source - this is a merit/sibling-position scholarship, income_criterion set to no-limit.

only_child_required is derived from 'the only child of her parents'. This is a hard gate that a category/income filter will not catch, so a student with siblings could still match on other criteria. Surface it as a visible eligibility line on the card.

schemes.name: National Education Policy 2020 (implementation framework)
schemes.ministry: Ministry of Education
schemes.implementing_body: Ministry of Education, UGC, AICTE, States/UTs
schemes.description: Comprehensive policy framework (not a single scheme) restructuring India's education system, including school curriculum (5+3+3+4), multiple entry-exit in higher education, multidisciplinary institutions, and the Academic Bank of Credits.
schemes.coverage_amount: Not applicable (policy framework, implemented via multiple downstream schemes)
schemes.eligibility: Not applicable (systemic policy)
schemes.target_beneficiaries: All learners across the education system
key_features: New 5+3+3+4 school curricular structure
Academic Bank of Credits (ABC) and multiple entry-exit options
Foundational Literacy and Numeracy focus (NIPUN Bharat)
Many other schemes (PM Vidyalaxmi, PM-USP, PM SHRI) implement NEP 2020 goals
schemes.notes: Included as a reference/framework entry since many active schemes are explicitly implementing NEP 2020 goals.
_review: Policy document. Excluded from student-facing results by default.

schemes.name: PM Schools for Rising India
schemes.ministry: Ministry of Education
schemes.description: Upgrades existing schools (government schools run by centre/states/UTs/local bodies) into exemplar institutions that showcase all components of NEP 2020, acting as mentor schools for others in their area.
schemes.coverage_amount: Institutional upgrade grants (not an individual benefit)
schemes.eligibility: Existing government/local-body schools selected via a challenge-mode process
schemes.target_beneficiaries: Students in selected PM SHRI schools; broader system via mentoring effect
key_features: Target of developing 14,500+ PM SHRI schools
Model schools for NEP 2020 implementation
Green school features, modern infrastructure, and ICT-enabled learning
_review: Selection is by school, not student. However students DO benefit by attending a selected school, so consider a 'school-level' display: a student can check whether their school is a PM SHRI school. That is a different lookup than a scholarship match.

schemes.name: PM eVIDYA
schemes.ministry: Ministry of Education
schemes.scheme_type: Central Sector Scheme (under Atmanirbhar Bharat Abhiyaan)
schemes.description: Unifies digital, online and on-air education initiatives to enable multi-mode and equitable access to education, launched in response to school closures during COVID-19.
schemes.coverage_amount: Free access to digital/broadcast educational content
schemes.eligibility: Universal - school and higher education students
schemes.target_beneficiaries: Students across school and higher education, including those without internet access (via TV/radio channels)
key_features: One Class-One Channel initiative on DIKSHA/SWAYAM PRABHA TV channels
QR-coded energised textbooks for all grades
Extension of digital content to visually/hearing impaired students

filter.disability_basis: Key feature states 'Extension of digital content to visually/hearing impaired students'.

_review: No cash benefit and no application. Card should read 'open to everyone' rather than showing an amount or an Apply button.

schemes.name: SWAYAM (Study Webs of Active Learning for Young Aspiring Minds)
schemes.ministry: Ministry of Education
schemes.description: National MOOC (massive open online course) platform offering free online courses from school to postgraduate level, integrated with academic credit recognition by UGC/AICTE.
schemes.coverage_amount: Free courses; nominal fee only for those opting for certification/proctored exam
schemes.eligibility: Universal - open to any learner
schemes.target_beneficiaries: School and higher education students, lifelong learners
key_features: Credit transfer recognised by UGC for up to a defined percentage of a degree programme
Courses across engineering, humanities, sciences, management, school subjects
Complemented by SWAYAM PRABHA DTH channels for regions with low internet access
_review: Registration is needed to take a course, so application_required is 'online' even though there is no eligibility gate and no competition. Distinguish 'register' from 'apply and compete' in the UI copy.

schemes.name: DIKSHA (Digital Infrastructure for Knowledge Sharing)
schemes.ministry: Ministry of Education
schemes.description: National platform for school education providing e-content, textbooks (via QR codes), and teacher training resources mapped to state and national curricula.
schemes.coverage_amount: Free access
schemes.eligibility: Universal - students, teachers, parents
schemes.target_beneficiaries: School students and teachers nationwide
key_features: Multilingual content across state boards and NCERT curriculum
QR-coded textbook linkage (Energised Textbooks)
Teacher training modules and certification
_review: No cash benefit. Multilingual content here is a strong asset for the multi-language requirement in the website spec - DIKSHA is arguably the right place to send users for translated material.

schemes.name: Skill India Mission (Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana)
schemes.ministry: Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship
schemes.description: Flagship skill certification scheme enabling youth to take industry-relevant skill training, with monetary reward on successful completion and assessment, to improve employability.
schemes.coverage_amount: Free short-term training; monetary reward/certification on successful assessment (amount varies by scheme phase)
schemes.eligibility: Indian youth (school/college dropouts and unemployed persons primarily); specific age criteria vary by component
schemes.target_beneficiaries: Unemployed youth, school/college dropouts, existing workers seeking recognition of prior learning
key_features: Short-Term Training (STT) and Recognition of Prior Learning (RPL) components
Delivered via Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Kendras (PMKKs)
Sector-specific skill councils define training standards
_review: Source says 'specific age criteria vary by component' and gives no income figure. income_criterion set to unstated - the eligibility text does imply a need/employment focus but no threshold is stated.
The monetary reward amount is explicitly 'varies by scheme phase' in the source. Do not print a number; link to the PMKVY portal.
Add a nearest-PMKK locator - this is the one scheme in the set where offline/in-person access genuinely matters.

schemes.name: National Apprenticeship Promotion Scheme
schemes.ministry: Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship
schemes.description: Promotes apprenticeship training by sharing part of the stipend cost with employers and reimbursing basic training costs, encouraging industry to engage apprentices.
schemes.coverage_amount: Government reimburses 25% of prescribed stipend (up to a cap) directly to apprentices; basic training cost reimbursement to Basic Training Providers
schemes.eligibility: Establishments engaging apprentices under the Apprentices Act, 1961; apprentices aged 14-35 depending on trade
schemes.target_beneficiaries: Youth undergoing apprenticeship training; employer establishments
key_features: Direct Benefit Transfer of stipend support to apprentices
Covers optional trade apprentices alongside designated trades
_review: The 25% figure is verbatim from the source. The source also says 'up to a cap' without stating the cap - do not present Rs. amount without it.
Route is: apprentice -> employer establishment -> portal. A student cannot self-apply. The card must say this or it will generate failed applications.

schemes.name: Jawahar Navodaya Vidyalaya Scheme
schemes.ministry: Ministry of Education
schemes.description: Runs a network of fully residential, co-educational schools (one per district as far as possible) providing quality modern education, with reservation for rural students, to talented children regardless of family income.
schemes.coverage_amount: Free education including boarding, lodging, textbooks and uniforms (nominal fee for Class IX-XII students from non-SC/ST/BPL/girl categories)
schemes.eligibility: Admission via Jawahar Navodaya Vidyalaya Selection Test (JNVST) for Class VI (and lateral entry to Class IX); minimum 75% seats reserved for rural students
schemes.target_beneficiaries: Talented children, mainly from rural areas, Class VI-XII
key_features: One JNV per district (target), fully residential
Reservation for SC/ST, girls, and children with disabilities as per norms
CBSE-affiliated curriculum

filter.disability_basis: Key feature states 'Reservation for SC/ST, girls, and children with disabilities as per norms'.

_review: Description explicitly says 'regardless of family income' - income_criterion is no-limit. This scheme should appear for every income band, which is the single most useful 'free education' result in the dataset.
The 'nominal fee for Class IX-XII' caveat means it is not unconditionally free. Show it.
JNVST is a competitive test with a rural-residency requirement. Neither is captured by the income/category filter.

schemes.name: Kendriya Vidyalaya Sangathan Scheme
schemes.ministry: Ministry of Education
schemes.description: Operates a nationwide chain of schools primarily to provide uniform, quality education for children of transferable central government employees (including defence and paramilitary personnel), with admission also open to other categories.
schemes.coverage_amount: Nominal tuition fee (free for girls up to Class XII in most KVs, and for SC/ST students at primary level per current norms)
schemes.eligibility: Priority to children of transferable central government/defence/paramilitary employees; remaining seats open to general public as per admission guidelines
schemes.target_beneficiaries: Children of central government employees and general public (residual seats)
key_features: 1,250+ Kendriya Vidyalayas across India and abroad
Common curriculum (CBSE) minimizing disruption from parental transfers
Admission via age-based criteria and priority categories, not entrance exam at primary level
_review: No income condition, but there IS an employment-priority condition that the filter set cannot express. Add a government_employee_household boolean or this will over-promise to the general public.
'1,250+' KV count and the fee-concession norms ('per current norms') are volatile - re-verify.

schemes.name: Eklavya Model Residential Schools Scheme
schemes.ministry: Ministry of Tribal Affairs
schemes.implementing_body: National Education Society for Tribal Students (NESTS)
schemes.description: Establishes residential schools for Scheduled Tribe (ST) students to provide quality education comparable to Navodaya Vidyalayas, aiming for at least one EMRS in every block with more than 50% ST population.
schemes.coverage_amount: Free residential education including boarding and lodging
schemes.eligibility: Scheduled Tribe students, primarily from Class VI onward
schemes.target_beneficiaries: Scheduled Tribe students in blocks with significant tribal population
key_features: Target of 740+ EMRS across India
CBSE-pattern curriculum with focus on preserving tribal culture and heritage
Managed centrally by NESTS since 2019 restructuring
_review: Fully free residential education with no income test - the strongest 'no income needed' result in the dataset, but only for ST students. The category filter is the only thing standing between a user and this scheme, so it must not be optional.
Availability is limited to blocks with >50% ST population. A user outside such a block will see this as a false positive. Consider a state/district field to check availability.

schemes.name: Central Sector Interest Subsidy Scheme
schemes.ministry: Ministry of Education (Dept. of Higher Education)
schemes.description: Provides full interest subsidy during the moratorium period (course duration plus one year, or 6 months after getting a job, whichever is earlier) on education loans for professional/technical courses in India, for economically weaker students. Now integrated with PM-USP.
schemes.coverage_amount: Full interest subsidy during moratorium period on loans up to Rs. 10 lakh
schemes.eligibility: Family income up to Rs. 4.5 lakh per annum; first-time borrower for professional/technical course in India under the Model Education Loan Scheme
schemes.target_beneficiaries: Economically weaker students taking education loans for professional/technical courses
key_features: Interest subsidy credited directly to the loan account
Applied for via the Vidya Lakshmi Portal / now PM Vidyalaxmi portal
One-time benefit, not available if already availing another interest subsidy scheme
_review: max_income 450000 derived verbatim from 'Family income up to Rs. 4.5 lakh per annum'.
id PMMVY-EDU-NOTE is a copy-paste artefact from the PMMVY (health) dataset. This is an education record. Rename to CSIS.

This record overlaps PM-USP, which the source itself states ('Now integrated with PM-USP'). Two separate cards for one benefit is confusing. Mark one as the parent and the other as subsumed rather than listing both as equal matches.
'One-time benefit, not available if already availing another interest subsidy scheme' is a hard exclusion. A student already on PM-USP will double-claim. Surface this on the card.
